summary.headline: Indian Bank Q4 FY26: Q4 net profit Rs 3,103 crore (+1.3% QoQ), FY26 profit Rs 12,156 crore (+11.33%), gross NPA cut to 1.98%.
summary.overview: Management described FY26 as a decent year, beating guidance on most parameters except cost-to-income, with advances up 13.43% led by RAM (+15.18%) and corporate growth reviving to 9.19%. Gross NPA fell 111 bps to 1.98% and annualised Q4 slippage eased to 0.85%, while NIM for the year declined 17 bps to 3.24%. Management guided FY27 to tighter NIM (3.10%-3.25%), ROA (1.20%-1.30%) and growth (advances 11%-13%), citing rising cost of deposits and lower treasury income. ECL impact was not quantified; management said it would be absorbed over one to three quarters and that the final guidelines were received only the day before the call.

financial_highlights.change: down from 46.90% in December; above guidance

financial_highlights.value: Rs 31,000 crore (SMA-0 ~Rs 16,000 cr, SMA-1 ~Rs 9,000 cr, SMA-2 ~Rs 6,000 cr)
About Rs 310 crore (management cited Rs 400-500 crore MOC in Q4)

segments.name: Retail (RAM)
segments.commentary: Retail grew 18.72% and MSME 16.39% within RAM (+15.18%); about 6 lakh loans and Rs 48,000 crore sanctioned to MSME. Personal loans only Rs 6,500 crore and MFI Rs 3,300 crore.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate advances grew 9.19% after about 3% last year; corporate sanctions about Rs 1.31 trillion. Exposure to NBFCs fell about Rs 8,000 crore, with about 99% rated AAA/AA/A.

segments.name: Overseas
segments.commentary: Overseas book runs through GIFT City and Singapore branches (plus Sri Lanka), mainly syndicated loans and trade finance across sectors.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: Digital business grew 63% to Rs 272,000 crore; mobile banking users 2.36 crore; 94% of transactions digital; 97% of retail and agri loans sanctioned digitally.

guidance_outlook: FY27 deposit growth 9%-11%; advances growth 11%-13%; CASA around 40%; CD ratio around 80%.
FY27 NIM 3.10%-3.25% (cost of deposits to stay elevated as advances outpace deposits); ROA 1.20%-1.30%.
FY27 gross NPA 1.50%-1.60%; net NPA below 0.25%; credit cost below 1%; slippage ratio below 1%.
FY27 recoveries Rs 4,500-5,500 crore (vs guidance Rs 5,500-6,500 crore in FY26); written-off book recovery Rs 1,200-1,500 crore.
Treasury profit expected around Rs 1,000-1,200 crore for FY27; LCR to be kept around 115%-120%.
ECL impact to be absorbed over roughly one to three quarters; management said some spill-over into FY28 is likely. Numbers to be given later.
Management said it is comfortable with growth 1%-2% below industry, prioritising NIM and asset quality.
capex_capacity: Opened 102 branches so far; target about 300 branches over three years, described as on track.
IND Optima cash management launched with 150-plus corporate customers onboarded.
Digital pipeline: corporate CRM, corporate ecosystem engine, RFP creator, invoice processing, intelligent document reader, IND UPI app upgrade, and automated suspicious transaction reporting.
Digital and IT budget to be roughly equivalent to employee cost, per Ashutosh Choudhury.
demand_pricing: Growth drivers: jewel loans (16%-17% of book, Rs 1.27 trillion) grew about 28% last year on gold price rises; management does not expect similar growth this year.
Around 50% of the loan book is linked to external benchmarks, leaving little repricing lever; MCLR-linked loans are the main remaining lever.
Retail term deposit rates will not be cut because bulk deposit rates are elevated; bulk and CD together are about 18%-19% of deposits, kept under 20%.
Pipeline Rs 51,000 crore, of which sanctioned but unavailed term loans about Rs 34,000-35,000 crore; focus on green energy, transmission, data centres and roads.
Textile remains stressed for about two years; management says little leather exposure.
Average SA balance (ex-BSBD) rose to Rs 46,000 from Rs 30,000; average current account balance rose to Rs 2.64 lakh from Rs 1.88 lakh.

qa_highlights.question: How prepared is the bank for the final ECL guidelines, and how large is the hit?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the final guidelines came the day before and impact will be a little higher than draft estimates, adding the HTM book is now included. It declined to give a number yet, saying it would give concrete figures later, and expects the impact to be absorbed over one to three quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Will the West Asia war and tariffs raise slippages? What about SMA trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q4 slippage rose on about Rs 400-500 crore of March MOC, which recurs each March. SMA fell mainly because two government accounts left SMA-2; management also said some stress has been present since tariffs in August but is not visible in SMA.

qa_highlights.question: How will treasury income trend?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said treasury will be lower but not as severe as last year, since securities have not been sold at low yields. It expects Rs 1,000-1,200 crore of treasury profit for FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bank measuring the revenue benefit of digital investments?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said benefits are real but not quantified; cited 94% digital transactions (branch visits cost at least 5x more), and said it will try to quantify going forward.

qa_highlights.question: What levers exist on the asset side if cost of deposits rises?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said few levers remain since about 50% of loans are external-benchmark linked; MCLR-linked loans may reprice up. It is focusing on mid-sized corporates of Rs 50-500 crore for better pricing.

qa_highlights.question: What is the LCR and why is it so high?
qa_highlights.answer: Average LCR was 127% (currently 123%-124%). Management said 115%-120% is a fair operating level and that excess SLR holdings support the ratio.

qa_highlights.question: What is the AFS reserve movement?
qa_highlights.answer: AFS reserve moved from about Rs 400 crore in December to minus Rs 200 crore in March, per management.

risks_watch: ECL transition: impact not quantified; some spill-over into FY28 expected; HTM book now included; management has not disclosed existing floating/standard provisions beyond about Rs 500 crore standard-asset provisions in Q4.
Cost of deposits rising with advances outpacing deposits; NIM guidance cut to 3.10%-3.25%.
Recoveries falling (Rs 7,600 crore to Rs 6,600 crore) and treasury income lower in FY27.
Cost-to-income ratio ended FY26 at 46.03%, above guidance; management said course correction is underway.
MSME stress if industry weakens; textile sector weak for about two years; monitor SMA-0 (up to about Rs 16,000 crore).
summary.management_tone: Confident on asset quality and profitability, with a clear message that growth is secondary to NIM and asset quality. Cautious and somewhat evasive on ECL quantum and on the cost-of-deposit outlook, saying numbers will come later.
key_quotes: So, if I summarize the result, I think it has been a decent year, almost all parameters except cost-to- income ratio, we have done better than our guidance.
But, having said that, let me assure you, all of you, that impact is not going to be very huge.
We will give you concrete numbers so that variation is minimum.
So, my focus is, of course, growth, but NIM and asset quality should also remain intact.
So, in NPA, in fact, we are not holding any floating provision, NPA whatever we are making only a specific account-wise provision.

adds.what: About 300 branches over three years (102 opened so far)

growth.why: FY27 advances growth guided at 11%-13% and deposits 9%-11%, backed by a sanctioned-but-unavailed term loan pipeline of about Rs 34,000-35,000 crore and a branch rollout (102 opened, ~300 targeted over three years), though no quantified capacity or order timing was given for the guidance itself.
